passage: Come son of Latona, golden-haired Apollo, whose will echoes the Father of Gods and men: illuminate my mind! Come Memory, wise queen, and awaken things learned long ago, things which beg to again come to light! Our minds are darkened with clouds and our hearts are downtrodden, tormented by mundane trials which never end. my hands that I might retrieve the marvelous narrative given to us long ago by the great theologian who sang with a lyre of gold, the genesis of the greatest of the blessed deathless Gods, those born from Earth and the blood of Heaven. Then these thoughts appeared in the ether of my mind, “Take the fragments scattered in the texts of those who unwittingly hid them. Arrange their content in a mighty poem, easy to understand for the pious, yet obscure to the profane, !
ref_text: In the beginning there was neither heaven nor earth, but only Time, who had no father, and with him the Aether and the boundless Chasm, and from these the silver egg was made.
